questions.enonce_markdown:
Describe the following with respect to Database Management Systems:

(a) Attributes. (2 marks)

(b) Data redundancy. (2 marks)

(c) Partial dependence. (1 mark)

(d) Primary key. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Attributes (2 marks).** The attributes are the **properties or characteristics of an entity**; in a relational table they are the **fields (columns)**. For example the entity STUDENT has the attributes StudentID, Name, DateOfBirth and Class, and each record gives a value for every attribute.

**(b) Data redundancy (2 marks).** The **unnecessary repetition (duplication) of the same data** in several places of a database or in several files. It wastes storage space and causes **inconsistencies** and update problems: if a customer's address is stored in five tables and is changed in only one, the data no longer agree. It is reduced by good design and by normalisation.

**(c) Partial dependence (1 mark).** A situation in which a **non-key attribute depends on only a part of a composite primary key** and not on the whole key. For example in ORDERLINE(OrderID, ProductID, ProductName, Quantity) with key (OrderID, ProductID), ProductName depends on ProductID alone. It is removed in second normal form (2NF).

**(d) Primary key (1 mark).** An attribute (or a combination of attributes) whose value **uniquely identifies each record** of a table; it can never be repeated or left empty (null). Example: StudentID in the STUDENT table.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is prototyping? (2 marks)

(b) Give TWO advantages of prototyping. (2 marks)

(c) At which stage in system development is prototyping done. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Prototyping (2 marks).** Prototyping is the building of an **early, simplified working model** of a system (or of a part of it, such as the screens and reports) which is shown to the users, tested and improved according to their comments, **before the final system is built**.

**(b) Two advantages (2 marks)** (any two):

1. The users **see and try the system early** and give feedback, so their real requirements are understood better.
2. Errors, omissions and misunderstandings are **found early**, when they are cheap to correct, which reduces the risk and the cost of changes later.
3. The **users are involved** in the development, so they accept the final system more easily.

**(c) Stage (1 mark).** Prototyping is done at the **system design stage**, after the requirements have been found in the analysis and before the full system is coded and implemented (it is also used at the end of analysis to confirm the requirements).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Differentiate between the following and give an example of each.

(a) Low level programming and high level programming. (4 marks)

(b) System software and application software. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Low level and high level programming (4 marks).**

| | Low level programming | High level programming |
|---|---|---|
| Closeness | Close to the hardware: instructions correspond (nearly) one-to-one with the processor's operations | Close to human language, with English-like words and mathematical notation |
| Portability | Machine dependent: a program for one type of processor does not run on another | Machine independent (portable): the same program can run on different computers after translation |
| Ease | Difficult to write, read and debug, the programmer must manage registers and memory | Easier and faster to write, read and maintain; one statement gives many machine instructions |
| Translation | Machine code needs none; assembly language needs an *assembler* | Needs a *compiler* or an *interpreter* |
| Speed | Very fast, uses little memory | Generally slower and larger |
| Example | Machine code, assembly language | Pascal, C, Python, Java |

**(b) System software and application software (2 marks).**

- **System software** manages and controls the computer hardware and provides a platform on which other programs run, for example an **operating system** (Windows, Linux), a utility program or a device driver.
- **Application software** carries out a specific task for the user, for example a **word processor** (Microsoft Word), a spreadsheet (Excel) or a web browser.
